name: SAM SIP
description: Sam Sip (Pa-Som Sip) is a draw-and-discard game from Thailand and Burma. Players draw from the stock or the previous player's discard, then discard one card. The aim is to be the first to hold three pairs: two cards totalling 10 (Ace=1), two 10s, or two equal picture cards (J, Q, K). Wild cards (jokers and cards matching the turned-up rank) can substitute for any card. The Thai name means "mixing tens".

Country/Region of Origin: Thailand and Burma
Time Period: Traditional; first Western description from Phuket area, May 2001
Historical Development: Draw and discard game; Thai name means "mixing tens"; played on islands off Phuket and in Burma
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Thailand and Burma

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4 or 5
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck plus three jokers (55 cards) in Phuket version; some variants use 52 cards without jokers.
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Three in main version; none in Korat, Bangkok, Burma variants

Standard 52-card deck (and three jokers for main version)
Table space; stakes agreed in advance if playing for money

Cards per Player: Five each
Dealing Pattern: Counter-clockwise, one card at a time
One card turned face up after the deal (wild indicator); remainder forms stock
